Listen to this article Share Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals has cleared its final major regulatory hurdle ahead of its landmark debut on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX). Advertisement Advertisement On Monday, November 23, Nigeria’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) officially approved the share allotment plan for the refinery’s heavily oversubscribed Initial Public Offering (IPO), which drew investor demand at roughly three times the initial 4.1 billion-share offer before closing in late October. This regulatory green light ends weeks of anticipation for retail and institutional subscribers, paving the way for Central Securities Clearing System (CSCS) share crediting, surplus refunds, and the start of public trading on the NGX. The offer, which closed last month, attracted demand roughly three times its original size. In response to strong investor appetite, the refinery also sought regulatory approval to expand the offer size by up to 30 percent. Marketed by Aliko Dangote, Africa’s richest man, as the “people’s IPO,” the transaction was structured to broaden domestic ownership and allow everyday Nigerians to share in the returns of the $20 billion facility. Retail participation was driven largely through fintech and digital investment platforms, where investors were able to subscribe for a minimum of 10 shares—equivalent to roughly $4. Dangote has also indicated plans for a potential secondary listing of the refining business in the United States within the next three to four years. Advertisement Located in the Lekki Free Zone on the outskirts of Lagos, the 700,000-barrel-per-day facility has reshaped Nigeria’s downstream petroleum sector since commencing operations in 2024, reducing the country’s reliance on imported refined products. The refinery has also capitalised on global supply disruptions linked to the conflict in Iran, boosting its export footprint—including jet fuel shipments to Western Europe. Management plans to double the plant’s refining capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day by 2029.
